The Regional Program Director, California is Juma's senior on\-the\-ground program leader for the Bay Area and Sacramento markets. This role owns the quality, consistency, and effectiveness of YouthConnect programming across both sites, and brings direct experience in workforce development along with genuine program design expertise. Strategically forecast and pace recruitment cycles to align with the seasonal hiring surges of regional stadium enterprise partners.

In 1922, Woodcraft Rangers opened its doors in Los Angeles and began its mission of guiding young people as they explore pathways to purposeful lives. Any person occupying a position under exempt appointment shall not be subject to civil service selection, appointment, and removal procedures. Exempt appointees are considered "at will" and shall serve at the discretion of the Appointing Officer.

**About the Port of San Francisco**


The Port of San Francisco is steward to one of the world’s most iconic waterfronts – a dynamic 7\.5\-mile stretch along the San Francisco Bay. With a diverse real estate portfolio, active maritime operations, and hundreds of tenants including Pier 39, the Ferry Building, Oracle Park, and the Exploratorium, the Port plays a central role in the city’s economic vitality, cultural identity, and global reputation. Our dedicated employees operate marinas and piers, maintain historic public spaces, and partner with the private sector to revitalize neighborhoods and deliver transformative development and open space projects.


Over the past decade, the Port has evolved into a strategically driven agency known for innovation, equity, and impact. Through bold initiatives in economic recovery, resilience, and public\-private partnerships, the Port has secured historic investments and created a strong foundation for the waterfront’s next chapter. With over $13\.5 billion in planned resilience infrastructure and more than 60 acres of new waterfront neighborhoods under development, the Port is leading the way in adapting San Francisco’s shoreline for future generations.


The Port’s mission is grounded in stewardship, partnership, and public service. We are building a workplace rooted in inclusion and belonging and shaping a waterfront where all are welcome. We invite you to join a team that is not only transforming the city’s shoreline but also setting a new standard for public sector excellence and innovation.


For more information about the Port of San Francisco, visit SFPort.com. Follow us on Twitter and Facebook.

The Port of San Francisco is comprised of eight divisions: Executive; Finance and Administration; Real Estate and Development; Maritime; Maintenance; Engineering; Planning and Environment; and the Waterfront Resilience Program. The Executive Director will retain direct management for the Executive and Finance and Administration divisions. The Assistant Port Director/Chief Operating Officer will be charged with overseeing the work program for the operating divisions: Real Estate and Development; Maritime; Maintenance; Engineering; and Planning and Environment. The Deputy Directors for each of these divisions will be direct reports to the Assistant Port Director/Chief Operating Officer. Because the Waterfront Resilience Program is at a key strategic point in its development as it pivots from conceptual planning to design of specific segments of the line of defense, the Executive Director and the Assistant Port Director will share management of this division for a period of time before it eventually transitions to the Assistant Port Director’s operating portfolio.


For more information on each of these divisions, please see our website at: https://www.sfport.com/about/divisions\-and\-staff

**The Executive Division**


The second key function for the Assistant Port Director/Chief Operating Officer is to contribute to the development and management of strategic direction for the full organization as a member of the Executive Division. The Executive Division reports directly to the Port Executive Director and includes the Assistant Port Director/Chief Operating Officer, Communications, Government Affairs, Equity, Inclusion \& Diversity, Security, Port Commission Secretary and the Port's General Counsel.

* **Security** is responsible for developing, directing, and implementing a comprehensive homeland security program for the Port and its emergency plans and procedures, in preparation for and in response to emergencies and disasters. The team is also charged with ensuring public safety along the waterfront including during major civic events.
* The **Port Commission Secretary** serves as Secretary to the Port Commission and Executive Assistant to the Port Executive Director.  **About Homeless Children’s Network (HCN)**



Since 1992, HCN has been San Francisco’s leading nonprofit agency for comprehensive early intervention and mental health support for underserved and historically marginalized children, youth, and families experiencing homelessness, housing instability, or living in intergenerational poverty. Our mobile therapeutic model is both accessible and scalable, enabling clinicians to meet clients directly in the community. As the hub of a Collaborative of 60\+ service agencies and community\-based organizations, we serve over 2,500 clients each year, reaching those most reluctant to trust conventional mental health systems. Central to our work is our Afri\-centric mental health and wellness model. This community\-defined approach addresses health inequities and the persistent cycle of racism and trauma over generations. This model not only uplifts the Black/African American communities but also strengthens the behavioral health outcomes of all San Franciscans, fostering resilience, healing, and lasting change.

 **KUPONA SUD OUTPATIENT PROGRAM OVERVIEW:**

  

Kupona Program is a culturally responsive and family\-centered substance use treatment program for youth in San Francisco. Utilizing Evidence\-based and locally\-innovative interventions, this program will provide co\-occurring or SUD standalone services for youth who are at risk or struggling with drug, alcohol, and other substances. Kupona offers a continuum of services depending on the level of care needed:


* Early Intervention for youth who are at risk of developing a Substance Use Disorder (SUD),
* Outpatient Level 1 for youth who are actively using substances and meet criteria for SUD diagnosis, but who present with NO acute intoxication and/or withdrawal potential.
* Intensive Outpatient for youth who are actively using substances, meet criteria for SUD diagnosis, and who present with acute intoxication and/or withdrawal potential.
* This program serves all ethnicities and populations within San Francisco with focused expertise to meet the needs of youth under the age of 18 years old who are Medi\-Cal beneficiaries.

  


**POSITION SUMMARY:**



The SUD Program Director is responsible for overseeing the day\-to\-day operations of HCN’s youth substance use disorder (SUD) treatment program, including clinical services, staff management, client care, compliance with regulations, and ensuring the delivery of high\-quality and evidence\-based treatment under the Drug Medi\-Cal (DMC\-ODS) framework. The SUD Program Director reports Directly to the COO

**Schedule:** Hybrid (at least 2 days per week on site)

The School of Humanities and Sciences (H\&S) is Stanford's largest school, with 24 top\-ranked academic departments and dozens of programs, centers, and institutes spanning the humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences. H\&S teaches the majority of undergraduates in its majors, trains roughly 40% of Stanford PhDs, and produces knowledge that adds to humanity’s inheritance. The school sits at the intellectual core of the university, and its faculty and students drive discovery across expansive fields of inquiry.


The H\&S Development team partners with the Dean's office, department chairs, center directors, and colleagues across University Development to secure philanthropic support for the school's most pressing priorities — from named professorships and graduate fellowships to research initiatives and capital projects. As H\&S works toward an ambitious fundraising goal amid a competitive philanthropic landscape, the team is focused on building a robust pipeline of new donors and deepening relationships with existing supporters.  

  



**Position Summary:**

The H\&S development team is seeking candidates for an Associate Director of Development, reporting to the Director of Development. This fundraiser role will be responsible for identifying, cultivating, and soliciting new donors to H\&S, with a primary focus on donor discovery. This is an excellent opportunity for a fundraiser who enjoys the front end of the philanthropic process — building relationships, uncovering giving capacity and interest, and helping shape a donor's philanthropic journey from the very first conversation.


This role will work from a robust pool of qualified prospects to build and manage a discovery\-focused major gift portfolio across a range of academic clusters within H\&S. The Associate Director will help manage the discovery pipeline across the team, working closely with fellow fundraisers and the Dean's office and supporting special projects that draw on fundraiser expertise.


We're looking for someone who is a naturally curious relationship\-builder, comfortable initiating conversations with new prospects and confident in representing Stanford's academic priorities to a broad range of donors. Familiarity with fundraising databases and tools is a plus, as is prior experience in higher education or nonprofit fundraising — though we welcome candidates from adjacent client\-facing or relationship\-driven fields who are eager to grow into development work. Comfort with AI\-enabled productivity tools is strongly encouraged.


  
**Core Duties** :


* Develop solicitation goals, objectives, and strategies for development projects and/or specific donor populations or geographic regions. Cultivate and solicit gifts to the university.
* Manage an active portfolio, and track solicitation assignments and progress. Work with a portfolio of assigned prospects to cultivate, solicit, and steward their support.
* Take responsibility for a wide range of fundraising activities, including maintaining an active level of contacts, identifying new prospective donors and volunteers, providing stewardship, and coordinating volunteer fundraising efforts.
* Stay informed on current university initiatives and activities.
* Develop relationships leading to gifts in the $250,000 \- $5,000,000 range.
* Enhance relationships between current and prospective major donors and the school or unit's faculty, students, dean, staff and volunteers.
* Work with staff, donors, volunteers, and other university staff to assist in establishing and maintaining relationships with all university constituencies.
* Design and manage appeals (e.g., direct mail, email, video, phone, and other channels) to target key populations to maximize fundraising potential.
* Establish ongoing relationships with individual alumni through personal visits, phone calls, and meaningful contacts.
* Prioritize prospects, prepare background information, make volunteer assignments as appropriate, and follow up with volunteers to ensure completion of assigned solicitations.
* Work closely with other colleagues in development to align program goals with the overall giving goals of the university’s development organization.

The ED is responsible for working with the organization’s partners to fulfill housing stability grant requests, identifying strategic partners, fundraising, coordinating with Cooper Tacia’s finance and marketing teams, and engaging with the community.

**Background**


Founded in 2023, the Cooper Charitable Foundation was created with the mission to improve people’s lives by helping them secure stable housing. John Cooper, our founder, and his family come from quite humble beginnings. Each of them understands the power of stability and safety in changing the trajectory of one's life. The Cooper Foundation was created to honor his own family and to express gratitude for his journey.


John learned about transitional housing grants while involved with Haven in Lee County, a non\-profit providing assistance to victims of domestic violence and sexual assault. The Cooper Charitable Foundation adapted this concept and created Housing Stability Grants to address the critical issue of housing accessibility in our communities.


Our grants provide financial assistance in two ways – helping working people access housing or preventing people from being evicted due to life circumstances.


The majority of our grants help people pay move\-in fees such as security deposits, utility deposits and first and last month’s rent. What we discovered is that many unsheltered people are working; they can pay their rent, but they can’t save enough money for the upfront fees required by most landlords. This is the biggest barrier to safe and accessible housing.


We also assist those who are working but cannot keep up with their monthly expenses due to life circumstances. Issues such as illness, mental health, a car accident, job loss, divorce or domestic violence can all impact people’s lives in different ways. We help people pay their rent and utilities or pay for car repairs or other expenses.

**Financial Management**

jobs.description:
Join an organization at the forefront of improving health by transforming care through Centering® groups  

Chief Executive Officer, Fractional  

General Description*Centering Healthcare Institute (CHI) is a 25\-year\-old 501(c)(3\) nonprofit organization whose mission is to champion and advance the evidence\-based Centering group model of care to transform how healthcare is practiced and experienced, empowering healthcare providers and patients to improve health outcomes. CHI partners with approximately 400\+ provider organizations across the U.S. to implement and sustain its three Centering group models of care \-CenteringPregnancy®, CenteringParenting ®, and CenteringHealthcare ®.*  

The Opportunity
Centering Healthcare Institute (CHI) stands at a defining moment in its evolution and in the national movement for maternal and reproductive health equity. With expanding partnerships, rising public and policy attention to group prenatal care, and growing opportunities to shape systems of care, CHI is poised to amplify its national impact and redefine how communities experience health and belonging.  

The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) will be a mission\-driven and visionary leader who brings both strategic foresight and a deep commitment to CHI’s purpose. More than a steward of operations, the CEO will be a systems thinker and catalyst—someone who thrives in complexity, leads with courage and curiosity, and builds enduring partnerships rooted in trust and shared accountability.  

CHI seeks a transformative governance leader who can inspire alignment across a distributed and diverse organization; cultivate relationships with funders, health systems, and policymakers; and guide CHI’s evolution into a more visible, connected, and resilient national platform for change. This leader will be ambitious yet grounded, collaborative yet decisive—balancing strategy with humanity and vision with execution.  

The CEO will shape and advance CHI’s overall strategy and organizational structure, partnering closely with a high\-performing executive leadership team. The CEO reports directly to the Board of Directors and serves as its key partner in governance, strategy, and sustainability.  

This role offers a rare opportunity to define the future of CHI, architecting a thriving, future\-ready organization that drives systemic impact in maternal and reproductive health. The CEO will work in close partnership with the Board, staff, and external allies to ensure that CHI’s mission, culture, and strategy are powerfully aligned for the years ahead.

The next CEO of CHI will be a strategic and values\-rooted systems leader who brings both heart and vision to the role. Rather than solely executing plans, this leader will define the horizon, cultivate shared purpose, mobilize partners, and shape the future of equitable care through influence, insight, and innovation. The CEO will guide the organization through growth and systems change, anchoring CHI’s mission in measurable outcomes for families and communities.  

The role oversees CHI’s strategic direction, organizational health, partnerships, financial sustainability, and influence across the healthcare landscape. Working closely with the Board of Directors and Executive Team, the CEO will ensure CHI’s programs, operations, and governance are aligned with a long\-term vision for scale, systems impact, and sustainable excellence.  

The CEO will steward CHI through its next phase of growth, optimizing infrastructure, ensuring operational alignment with mission and strategy, and empowering leaders across the organization to thrive. This includes championing continuous improvement and change management across systems, partnerships, and culture to position CHI as a model for equity centered healthcare innovation.  

As the organization’s chief steward, the CEO will ensure that CHI’s operations, programs, and governance adhere to the highest standards of transparency, accountability, and performance. They will represent CHI nationally, building trust, visibility, and influence with policymakers, funders, health systems, and community partners.  

As a member of and leader for the Executive Team, the CEO will foster collaboration, promote excellence, and strengthen the organization’s capacity for innovation, advocacy, and sustained impact. Reporting to the CEO is the Chief Financial Officer, Chief External Engagement/Chief of Philanthropy Officer, Chief Operating Officer/Chief People \& Culture Officer.  

The strategic leader stepping into this role has an opportunity to set a clear vision and direction for CHI’s future, guiding the organization into a new era of relevance, reach, and systems\-level influence.

The Volunteer Center of Washington County is a mission\-driven organization empowering people for social good. Our programs are focused on inspiring, educating, engaging, and empowering volunteers to help our 55\+ local nonprofit partners.



The Executive Director role is a full\-time, salaried, exempt position which reports to the full Board of Directors. The intention of the position is to grow the organization, provide vision and strategy around future organizational needs, and strengthen staff capacity while enhancing our organizational culture. The Executive Director upholds our values and brings the energy and eagerness required to move our mission forward. The Executive Director serves as the chief executive officer of the organization and serves as the primary liaison to the Board of Directors.

* Innovative, bold, and ambitious. The Volunteer Center is a highly driven organization and we’re constantly innovating to support our local nonprofit partners. The Executive Director needs to be a strong, but thoughtful decision\-maker.

Responsibilities of the position:



Vision \& Strategy


* Strategic Vision. Lead the senior leadership team in the development and implementation of the strategic plan. * Fund Development. Lead the direction and empower the team on fundraising activities, including maintaining and growing donor relationships, assisting with event planning and execution, attending and speaking at community engagements, grant writing and proposal development. Work with the Board of Directors and staff to create new earned\-income streams while supporting already established revenue sources.


Financial Management


* Budget and Financial Accountability. Prepare and recommend the annual operating budget to the Board of Directors for approval. Execute on the approved budget, monitor and communicate monthly status to the Finance Committee and Board of Directors. Provide recommendations for any major investments or expenditures that fall outside of the annual operating budget (i.e. capital expenditures or new opportunities for growth). Lead any outside accounting and auditing partner relationships and manage expectations on all contracted services.
* Staff Benefits and Payroll Management. Responsible for establishing wages/pay rates and administering the payroll function, including oversight reporting for the Board Treasurer. Administering the Simple IRA program and ensuring all stated benefits (PTO, Holiday Pay) adhere to employment policies as stated in the Employee Handbook.


Staff Development


* Inspiring Leadership. Provide effective and thoughtful leadership by building strong relationships with stakeholders at all levels of the organization including staff, volunteers, business partners, donors, the general community, and the Board of Directors while continually reinforcing the Volunteer Center’s mission, vision, and values.
* Staff Growth. Work with the team leaders to ensure recruitment, interviewing, and selection of key roles support the needs of our growing organization. Work in collaboration with team leaders to ensure a positive experience for new employees and existing team members. Lead and collaborate with the team on annual team goal setting and conduct performance evaluations, as necessary. Lead development conversations to ensure staff is encouraged and empowered to expand their role and contributions to the organization and personal experiences.

Provide training and development opportunities for staff to enhance professional capabilities and career growth. Help build a cohesive, relationship\-driven work environment where each team member is recognized for their successes, contributions, and celebrated for their achievements, milestones. Attend continuing education opportunities, conferences, and/or summits annually to stay abreast of nonprofit management trends, processes, and best practices.

Ensure our space is used effectively to drive social good with a balance of community, nonprofit partnership collaborative efforts, and private revenue\-driving opportunities.

**IMCI** **Overview**
=====================




It’s My Community Initiative (IMCI) is a 501 (c)(3\) non\-profit organization in Oklahoma City with a mission of developing and expanding efforts to strengthen communities by building strong, healthy families. IMCI spearheads community projects, tackling issues of health, education, and employment, in partnership with other community\-based organizations and through programs funded by corporate partners, federal, state, and local governments, and philanthropic organizations.




IMCI offers programs that serve a number of special population groups, including the historically unemployed or underemployed, individuals with a criminal background including those reentering communities from incarceration, incumbent workers, veterans and low\-skilled or low\-wage workers. IMCI also works with TRUE Dads and Safe Families Oklahoma. TRUE Dads is a free program in Oklahoma City that helps dads be the kind of father they want to be. The Director of Major Gifts will lead the program, establishing and monitoring ambitious goals, and guide a mature and well\-structured team to achieve these goals. The ED is responsible for working with the organization’s partners to fulfill housing stability grant requests, identifying strategic partners, fundraising, coordinating with Cooper Tacia’s finance and marketing teams, and engaging with the community.

**Background**


Founded in 2023, the Cooper Charitable Foundation was created with the mission to improve people’s lives by helping them secure stable housing. John Cooper, our founder, and his family come from quite humble beginnings. Each of them understands the power of stability and safety in changing the trajectory of one's life. The Cooper Foundation was created to honor his own family and to express gratitude for his journey.


John learned about transitional housing grants while involved with Haven in Lee County, a non\-profit providing assistance to victims of domestic violence and sexual assault. The Cooper Charitable Foundation adapted this concept and created Housing Stability Grants to address the critical issue of housing accessibility in our communities.


Our grants provide financial assistance in two ways – helping working people access housing or preventing people from being evicted due to life circumstances.


The majority of our grants help people pay move\-in fees such as security deposits, utility deposits and first and last month’s rent. This is the biggest barrier to safe and accessible housing.


We also assist those who are working but cannot keep up with their monthly expenses due to life circumstances.
